registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered on his instruction to close the predictive econometrics gaps, before any run of this test
hypothesis: A dynamic factor nowcast of quarterly real GDP growth (q/q), made 30 days after the quarter ends (one common factor of the monthly indicators published by then, read with a Kalman filter and smoother, two-step method of Doz, Giannone and Reichlin 2011; GDP growth bridged on the quarter's average factor and last quarter's growth), has a lower RMSE than the historical mean of GDP growth published by then.
knownLimits: Few monthly series per country in the free data (activity index, leading indicator, inflation, policy rate; two to four), far fewer than the dozens a central bank factor model uses; the test asks whether even this small factor helps.
Same lags, countries, quarters, benchmark and pass mark as gdp_nowcast v1, so the two compare like for like.
One factor; loadings and the factor's AR(1) from principal components on months with every series published, then fixed in the Kalman filter (two-step), not iterated to maximum likelihood.
